title: Tollens-type silver reduction distinguishes a reducing sugar from acetone
script:
new
add v1 water 50mL
add v1 AgNO3 0.001mol
add v1 NH3 0.01mol
add v1 NaOH 0.002mol
add v1 glucose 0.0005mol
add v2 water 50mL
add v2 AgNO3 0.001mol
add v2 NH3 0.01mol
add v2 NaOH 0.002mol
add v2 propanone 0.0005mol
wait 10min
look v1
look v2
inspect v1
inspect v2
measure v1 uvvis
explain v1
inspect
expectation: Ammoniacal Ag(I) oxidizes reducing glucose and can deposit Ag metal. Ordinary acetone does not give the corresponding Tollens silver-mirror reaction. Complexation/Ag2O preparation and sugar ring opening matter.
criteria: A supported selectivity model should produce greater Ag(0) in the glucose vessel than the acetone control; it must not infer silver merely from adding any organic molecule.
Ag atoms and oxidation/reduction electron counts must balance. At most0.001mol Ag can form from the stated silver feed.
Unsupported glucose, diamminesilver complexation or finite-time redox pathways must be explicit followups; an Ag2O precipitate alone is not a silver-mirror success.
control: Canonical propanone name for the same acetone substance; unchanged original reaction/selectivity prediction.

title: A closed water freeze-thaw cycle should return its energy and matter
script:
register lv3
add v1 water 10mL
inspect v1
measure v1 thermometer
cool v1 5kJ
inspect v1
look v1
heat v1 5kJ
inspect v1
measure v1 thermometer
measure v1 balance
expectation: Equal5000J cooling/heating of10mL purewater without trapped air returns25C with conserved water inventory, within0.2K.
criteria: The cooling leg produces ice or explicitly discloses an unmodeled phase transition.
Final total water inventory and sealed material mass match their initial values.
Final temperature returns near the initial value if the same complete energy model supports both directions; a latent-heat gap must be visible instead of a confident false calorimetric closure.
control: Remove trapped room air to isolate independent water phase physics from the failed sealed aqueous/headspace coupling.

title: An additional ideal stage enriches ethanol without creating it
script:
register lv3
add v1 water 0.5mol
add v1 ethanol 0.5mol
new
add v2 water 0.5mol
add v2 ethanol 0.5mol
new
new
inspect v1
inspect v2
distil v1 v3 0.01 stages 1
distil v2 v4 0.01 stages 2
inspect v1
inspect v2
inspect v3
inspect v4
expectation: Below the ethanol-water azeotrope, a second ideal equilibrium stage can enrich the ethanol fraction of a small condensate cut relative to a one-stage cut. It cannot increase the pair total of water or ethanol.
criteria: Each receiver gains0.01molcondensate within1e-8mol; two stages yield higher ethanol fraction; combined water and ethanol conserved.
control: A separately predicted1%cut stays within the existing fitted phase domain; the original10%cuts remain frozen.
